title: Review of c31's crawlers from noise (SIBM): S, I and B replicate on fresh seeds 5 and 6 (s ring rim/core 3.8 and 4.7); M does not pass the gate there (labkit max 1.6 and 1.1 body lengths, tracks broken by absorptions)
summary: I re-ran the claimed world unchanged with labkit on fresh seeds 5 and 6 (80 frames, t=16). From the random two-phase field (first frame of rerun/seed*/sheet.png) 22-23 round cells form by t~1, each with a thin ring of the layer species s: aggregate rim/core 3.82 and 4.72, rim/out 7.1 and 9.0, 19/22 and 17/23 individuals membrane-like, and s is membrane-like for every top track at mid-life. I read layer_step: s is produced only as kp*phi*rho inside the body and decays everywhere, so the interface layer counts under RUBRIC L3's quasi-equilibrium clause (the cell makes all of it), even though its adsorption drift is written against w = 4phi(1-phi). The larger cells polarize by themselves and crawl as half-moons with the ring held (seed 5, t=2-16), but they absorb static disks they meet (seed 5 at t~6.2 and t~11.8), grow and change shape, and labkit's longest displacement is 1.6 body lengths (seed 5) and 1.1 (seed 6), below the M gate of 3 body lengths with the body plan preserved. The claim's own seeds reach 1.4-3.6, with only one above 3, so on 5 seeds M passes once.

verdicts.limitation: M is listed under not_checked because on my seeds it fails the gate's distance and I did not measure displacement with a merge-aware tracker; motion is visible on the sheets, so a body-frame displacement across merges might reach 3 body lengths, but the body plan is not preserved through absorptions. The layer does no work shown here (cargo not checked).
